prompt:
Some invoices need manual adjustments after checkout - a one-off surcharge or discount that finance applies by hand. Today those adjustments are nowhere in the finance summaries, so admin reports show the wrong amount still owed. Add adjustment-aware invoice summaries. Introduce an Adjustment record with a signed amountCents (positive is a surcharge, negative is a discount), a reason, and a createdAt timestamp, recorded against an order. Then expose an invoice summary, one row per invoice, with the fields orderId, grossCents, adjustmentsCents, paidCents and dueCents, such that grossCents + adjustmentsCents - paidCents equals dueCents. Invoices that have no adjustments must behave exactly as before, and the existing admin report fields must be preserved.

Wire the feature through the existing dependency Container (app/Container.php) so it can be driven programmatically, using these exact public names: a Container property `adjustmentService` whose method `add($orderId, $amountCents, $reason)` records and returns the Adjustment; a Container property `adjustmentsRepo` whose method `findByOrder($orderId)` returns the recorded Adjustment objects for that order (each object exposing public `amountCents`, `reason`, and `createdAt`); and an `App\Services\InvoiceService` method `summary()` that takes no arguments and returns an array with one row per invoice carrying the fields named above.
issue_title: Finance needs invoice summaries to include manual adjustments.
issue_body:
Some invoices need manual adjustments after checkout - a one-off surcharge or discount that finance applies by hand. Today those adjustments are nowhere in the finance summaries, so admin reports show the wrong amount still owed. Add adjustment-aware invoice summaries. Introduce an Adjustment record with a signed amountCents (positive is a surcharge, negative is a discount), a reason, and a createdAt timestamp, recorded against an order. Then expose an invoice summary, one row per invoice, with the fields orderId, grossCents, adjustmentsCents, paidCents and dueCents, such that grossCents + adjustmentsCents - paidCents equals dueCents. Invoices that have no adjustments must behave exactly as before, and the existing admin report fields must be preserved.

Wire the feature through the existing dependency Container (app/Container.php) so it can be driven programmatically, using these exact public names: a Container property `adjustmentService` whose method `add($orderId, $amountCents, $reason)` records and returns the Adjustment; a Container property `adjustmentsRepo` whose method `findByOrder($orderId)` returns the recorded Adjustment objects for that order (each object exposing public `amountCents`, `reason`, and `createdAt`); and an `App\Services\InvoiceService` method `summary()` that takes no arguments and returns an array with one row per invoice carrying the fields named above.
expected_behavior: An Adjustment record carries a signed amountCents, a reason, and a createdAt, and is recorded against an order.
A positive adjustment raises the amount due; a negative adjustment lowers it; multiple adjustments net together.
The invoice summary exposes orderId, grossCents, adjustmentsCents, paidCents and dueCents, and grossCents + adjustmentsCents - paidCents reconciles to dueCents.
Invoices with no adjustments behave exactly as before and the existing admin report fields are unchanged.
The feature is reachable via the Container as adjustmentService->add($orderId, $amountCents, $reason), adjustmentsRepo->findByOrder($orderId), and InvoiceService::summary().
expected_failure_summary: The baseline has no adjustment concept and no summary output: there is no Adjustment record, no store for adjustments, and InvoiceService exposes no adjustment-aware per-invoice summary, so adjustments never reach the reported balances.
task_author_notes: Stage 1 of the paygate_adjustments group. Reference adds an Adjustment domain type (signed amountCents + reason + createdAt), an AdjustmentRepository backed by a new Database->adjustments map, an AdjustmentService to record them, and an adjustment-aware InvoiceService::summary() that folds due from signed components (gross + adjustments - paid). Modelling due as a sum of signed components - not hardcoded arithmetic - makes Stage 2 (refunds) a symmetric extension; a hardcoded summary forces a rewrite, measured as extension friction.
